parts.article:
The dingo debate
 
Graziers see them as pests, and poisoning is common, but some biologists think Australia's dingoes are the best weapon in a war against imported cats and foxes.
 
A A plane flies a slow pattern over Carlton Hill station, a 3,600 square kilometre ranch in the Kimberley region in northwest Australia. As the plane circles, those aboard drop 1,000 small pieces of meat, one by one, onto the scrubland below, each piece laced with poison; this practice is known as baiting. Besides 50,000 head of cattle, Carlton Hill is home to the dingo, Australia's largest mammalian predator and the bane of a grazier's (cattle farmer's) life. Stuart McKechnie, manager of Carlton Hill, complains that graziers' livelihoods are threatened when dingoes prey on cattle. But one man wants the baiting to end, and for dingoes to once again roam Australia's wide-open spaces. According to Chris Johnson of James Cook University, “Australia needs more dingoes to protect our biodiversity.”
 
B About 4,000 years ago, Asian sailors introduced dingoes to Australia. Throughout the ensuing millennia, these descendants of the wolf spread across the continent and, as the Tasmanian tiger disappeared completely from Australia, dingoes became Australia's top predators. As agricultural development took place, the European settlers found that they could not safely keep their livestock where dingoes roamed. So began one of the most sustained efforts at pest control in Australia's history. Over the last 150 years, dingoes have been shot and poisoned, and fences have been used in an attempt to keep them away from livestock. But at the same time, as the European settlers tried to eliminate one native pest from Australia, they introduced more of their own.
 
C In 1860, the rabbit was unleashed on Australia by a wealthy landowner and by 1980 rabbits had covered most of the mainland. Rabbits provide huge prey base for two other introduced species: the feral (wild) cat and the red fox. The interaction between foxes, cats and rabbits is a huge problem for native mammals. In good years, rabbit numbers increase dramatically, and fox and cat populations grow quickly in response to the abundance of this prey. When bad seasons follow, rabbit numbers are significantly reduced – and the dwindling but still large fox and cat populations are left with little to eat besides native mammals.
 
D Australian mammals generally reproduce much more slowly than rabbits, cats and foxes – an adaption to prevent overpopulation in the arid environment, where food can be scarce and unreliable – and populations decline because they can't grow fast enough to replace animals killed by the predators. Johnson says dingoes are the solution to this problem because they keep cat and fox populations under control. Besides regularly eating the smaller predators, dingoes will kill them simply to lessen competition. Dingo packs live in large, stable territories and generally have only one fertile female, which limits their rate of increase. In the 4,000 years that dingoes have been Australia, they have contributed to few, if any, extinctions, Johnson says.
 
E Reaching out from a desolate spot where three states meet, for 2,500 km in either direction, is the world's longest fence, two meters high and stretching from the coast in Queensland to the Great Australian Bight in South Australia; it is there to keep dingoes out of southeast, the fence separates the main types of livestock found in Australia. To the northwest of the fence, cattle predominate; to the southwest, sheep fill the landscape. In fact, Australia is a land dominated by these animals – 25 million cattle, 100 million sheep and just over 20 million people.
 
F While there is no argument that dingoes will prey on sheep if given the chance, they don't hunt cattle once the calves are much past two or three weeks old, according to McKechnie. And a study in Queensland suggests that dingoes don't even prey heavily on the newborn calves unless their staple prey disappears due to deteriorating conditions like drought. This study, co-authored by Lee Allen of the Robert Wicks Research Centre in Queensland, suggests that the aggressive baiting programs used against dingoes may actually be counter-productive for graziers. When dingoes are removed from an area by baiting, the area is recolonized by younger, more solitary dingoes. These animals aren't capable of going after large prey like kangaroos, so they turn to calves. In their study, some of the highest rates of calf predation occurred in areas that had been baited.
 
G Mark Clifford, general manager of a firm that manages over 200,000 head of cattle, is not convinced by Allen's assertion. Clifford says, “It's obvious if we drop or loosen control on dingoes, we are going to lose more calves.” He doesn't believe that dingoes will go after kangaroos when calves are around. Nor is he persuaded of dingoes' supposed ecological benefits, saying he is not convinced that they manage to catch cats that often, believing they are more likely to catch small native animals instead.
 
H McKechnie agrees that dingoes kill the wallabies (small native animals) that compete with his cattle for food, but points out that in parts of Western Australia, there are no foxes, and not very many cats. He doesn't see how relaxing controls on dingoes in his area will improve the ecological balance. Johnson sees a need for a change in philosophy on the part of graziers. “There might be a number of different ways of thinking through dingo management in cattle country,” he says. “At the moment, though, that hasn't got through to graziers. There's still just one prescription, and that is to bait as widely as possible.”

questions.question: a description of a barrier designed to stop dingoes, which also divides two kinds of non-native animals

analyses.content: “Barrier” 对应 “fence”，“Divides two kinds of non-native animals” 对应 “separates... cattle... sheep”。

(Paragraph E) “...is the world's longest fence... it is there to keep dingoes out... the fence separates the main types of livestock... cattle predominate; to the southwest, sheep fill the landscape.”
题目提到一种旨在阻挡野狗的屏障描述，它也分隔了两种非本土动物。原文E段描述了世界上最长的“fence（围栏/屏障）”，它的存在是为了把野狗挡在东南部之外（keep dingoes out），并且分隔了“cattle（牛）”和“sheep（羊）”这两种主要的非本土牲畜。

questions.question: how dingoes ensure that rival species do not dominate

analyses.content: 题目说野狗如何确保竞争物种不占主导地位。原文D段提到Johnson说野狗是解决问题的办法，因为它们使猫和狐狸的种群“under control（受到控制）”，并且会为了“lessen competition（减少竞争）”而杀死它们。
“Ensure that rival species do not dominate” 对应 “keep cat and fox populations under control”。
(Paragraph D) “Johnson says dingoes are the solution... because they keep cat and fox populations under control.”

questions.question: a reference to a widespread non-native species that other animals feed on

analyses.content: 题目提到一种分布广泛的非本土物种，其他动物以其为食。原文C段提到1860年释放了“rabbit（兔子）”，到1980年覆盖了大部分大陆（widespread），并为狐狸和猫提供了巨大的“prey base（猎物基础/食物来源）”。
“Widespread non-native species” 对应 “rabbit... unleashed... covered most of the mainland”。
(Paragraph C) “In 1860, the rabbit was unleashed... Rabbits provide huge prey base for two other introduced species...”

questions.question: a mention of the dingo's arrival in Australia

analyses.content: “Arrival” 对应 “introduced... to Australia”。
题目提到野狗到达澳大利亚。原文B段开头明确说“About 4,000 years ago, Asian sailors introduced dingoes to Australia（大约4000年前，亚洲水手将野狗引入澳大利亚）”。
(Paragraph B) “About 4,000 years ago, Asian sailors introduced dingoes to Australia.”

questions.question: research which has proved that dingoes have resorted to eating young livestock

analyses.content: 题目提到证明野狗转而吃幼小牲畜的研究。原文F段提到Lee Allen的“study（研究）”表明，当野狗被诱杀后，年轻的野狗重占领地，它们无法捕食大猎物，所以“turn to calves（转向小牛/幼畜）”。
“Research which has proved” 对应 “This study... suggests... in their study... rates of calf predation occurred”。
(Paragraph F) “This study... suggests... so they turn to calves.”

questions.question: a description of a method used to kill dingoes

analyses.content: 题目提到一种用于杀死野狗的方法的描述。原文A段详细描述了飞机投下系有毒药的肉块，这种做法被称为“baiting（诱杀）”。
“Method used to kill” 对应 “baiting / drop... meat... laced with poison”。
(Paragraph A) “...drop 1,000 small pieces of meat... each piece laced with poison; this practice is known as baiting.”

questions.question: the way that the structure of dingo groups affects how quickly their numbers grow

analyses.content: (Paragraph D) “Dingo packs... generally have only one fertile female, which limits their rate of increase.”
“Structure of dingo groups” 对应 “generally have only one fertile female”，“How quickly... grow” 对应 “rate of increase”。
题目说野狗群体的结构影响其数量增长速度的方式。原文D段提到野狗群通常只有“one fertile female（一只可繁殖的雌性）”，这“limits their rate of increase（限制了它们的增长率）”。

questions.question: Dingoes tend to hunt native animals rather than hunting other non-native predators.

analyses.content: 题目说野狗倾向于捕食本土动物而不是其他非本土捕食者。原文G段 Mark Clifford 说他不相信野狗能经常抓到猫，认为它们“more likely to catch small native animals instead（更可能抓捕小型本土动物作为替代）”。
“Hunt native animals rather than... non-native predators” 对应 “more likely to catch small native animals instead [of cats]”。
(Paragraph G) “Clifford says... believing they are more likely to catch small native animals instead.”

questions.question: The presence of dingoes puts the income of some people at risk.

analyses.content: 题目说野狗的存在使一些人的收入面临风险。原文A段 Stuart McKechnie 抱怨说当野狗捕食牛时，牧场主的“livelihoods are threatened（生计受到威胁）”。
“Income... at risk” 对应 “livelihoods are threatened”。虽然Clifford也提到了损失小牛，但A段McKechnie的表述更直接对应“livelihood/income”这个概念。
(Paragraph A) “Stuart McKechnie... complains that graziers' livelihoods are threatened...”

questions.question: Dingoes have had little impact on the dying out of animal species in Australia.

analyses.content: (Paragraph D) “Johnson says... they have contributed to few, if any, extinctions.”
题目说野狗对澳大利亚动物物种的灭绝影响很小。原文D段 Chris Johnson 说在野狗存在的4000年里，它们“contributed to few, if any, extinctions（几乎没有导致任何灭绝）”。
“Little impact on the dying out” 对应 “contributed to few... extinctions”。

analyses.content: 题目说野狗取代了____成为澳大利亚的主要捕食动物。原文B段提到随着“Tasmanian tiger（塔斯马尼亚虎/袋狼）”完全消失，野狗成为了澳大利亚的顶级捕食者。
“Replaced” 对应原文的 “as the ... disappeared ... dingoes became...”。
(Paragraph B) “...as the Tasmanian tiger disappeared completely from Australia, dingoes became Australia's top predators.”
题目说当____较少时，狐狸和猫更可能捕食本土动物。原文C段提到当“rabbit numbers（兔子数量）”显著减少时，狐狸和猫只剩下本土哺乳动物可以吃。
“When there are fewer” 对应 “numbers are significantly reduced”。注意复数形式 rabbits。
(Paragraph C) “...when bad seasons follow, rabbit numbers are significantly reduced... left with little to eat besides native mammals.”
题目说澳大利亚动物繁殖速度慢是一种避免____的自然方式。原文D段提到这是一种适应，旨在干旱环境中“prevent overpopulation（防止人口过剩/过度繁殖）”。
“Avoiding” 对应 “prevent”。
(Paragraph D) “...an adaption to prevent overpopulation in the arid environment...”
